That said, cultural practices can indeed shape our subjective experience of time. For example, in some traditional societies, people might be more active during the night due to agricultural or social reasons. This doesn't necessarily mean they think the day starts at night, but rather that their daily rhythms are adapted to their environment and lifestyle.

This idea ties into the field of chronobiology, which studies the biological, environmental, and psychological aspects of time perception and sleep-wake cycles.
